newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan commodity futures may face problems - trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan commodity futures may face problems - trade.

text.p: Commodity futures are likely to face more hurdles than financial contracts when Taiwan opens its first futures exchange in late 1997, experts said on Wednesday.

Taiwan bullion and metals dealers said they expected to see little demand for base and precious metals futures and doubted whether such contracts would find sufficient trading volume to be viable in the market.
"Volume for local metals and precious metals futures will remain small, making local futures contracts unattractive," a gold dealer at Taiwan's Central Trust of China said.
Futures traders said they expected volume to be low because Taiwan lacked an established physical metals market.
Taiwan has no significant mine resources, relying solely on imports from overseas suppliers and buying primarily to meet its physical production needs.

Taiwan gold futures contracts, if launched, would probably attract little or no trading volume, a situation already seen for gold futures in Hong Kong and Singapore, the Central Trust of China dealer said.
Futures traders said launching commodity futures contracts would require further work on Taiwan's basic market structure for physical products delivery.
"Storage and transportation requirements make physical commodity delivery difficult," one said.

They said soybeans and corn were the only commodities with a high chance for successful futures trading in Taiwan, citing the island's large but unsophisticated physical market and its huge annual imports.

Taiwan, one of the world's major grain and oilseeds buyers, imported over 6.5 million tonnes of U.S. corn and 2.5 million tonnes of U.S. soybeans in 1996 for its huge food processing sector, traders said.
Taiwan's parliament on Tuesday adopted a long-delayed Futures Trading Law, clearing the way to open the island's first futures exchange as soon as October.
Securities and Exchange Commission officials expected the first item to be traded would be contracts linked to the benchmark TAIEX index of the main Taiwan Stock Exchange.
The stock index futures would be followed by the launch of commodity-related contracts.
